text: The complex that can show optical activity is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An octahedral complex is optically active only when it has no mirror plane, so that it is non-superimposable on its mirror image.

In $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{-}$ (type $\mathrm{MA}{}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{4}$), both the cis and the trans isomers contain a mirror plane through the metal and both $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ ligands, so neither is optically active.

In trans-$[\mathrm{CrCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{ox}){}_{2}]{}^{3-}$ the two oxalate rings lie in one plane with the two $\mathrm{Cl}$ ligands above and below it; that plane is a mirror plane, so the complex is optically inactive.

In cis-$[\mathrm{CrCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{ox}){}_{2}]{}^{3-}$ (type $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA}){}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{2}]$) the two chelate rings are arranged like the blades of a propeller and no mirror plane is present, so the complex exists as a pair of non-superimposable d and l forms.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Of the species, NO, NO$^{+}$, NO$^{2+}$ and NO$^{-}$
, the one with minimum bond strength is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Note : 

(1) $\, ~$ Bond strength $\propto$ Bond order 

(2) $\, ~$ Bond length $\propto$ $\frac{1}{Bondorder}$

(3) [MATH$_$FAILED] Bond order $=\frac{1}{2}$ [$N_{b}$ $-$ $N_{a}$] 

$N_{b} =$ No of electrons in bonding molecular orbital 

$N_{a}$ $=$ No of electrons in anti bonding molecular orbital

(4) $\, ~$ upto 14 electrons, molecular orbital configuration is 


[IMG]


Here $N_{a} =$ Anti bonding electron $=$ 4 and $N_{b} = 10$

(5) $\, ~$ After 14  electrons to 20 electrons molecular orbital configuration is - - -


[IMG]


Molecular orbital configuration of NO (15 electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{o}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 5$ 

$\therefore \quad$  BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-5]$ = 2.5

Similarly Molecular orbital configuration of NO$^{+} (14$ electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 4$

$\therefore \quad$  BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-4]$ = 3

Similarly Molecular orbital configuration of NO$^{2+} (13$ electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 9$

$N_{a} = 4$

$\therefore \quad$  BO = $\frac{1}{2}[9-4]$ = 2.5

Molecular orbital configuration of NO$^{-} (16$ electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 6$

$\therefore \quad$  BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-6]$ = 2

As Bond strength $\propto$ Bond order

$\therefore$ NO$^{–}$ will have minimum bond strength.

text:
The electronic spectrum of [$Ti(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$^{3+}$ shows a single broad peak with a maximum at $20,300 cm^{-1}$
.
The crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) of the complex ion, in kJ mol$^{-1}$, is :
(1 kJ mol$^{-1} = 83.7 cm^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Ti}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{1}$, so in the octahedral field of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ the electron occupies $t_{2g}$ ($t_{2g}^{1}e_{g}^{0}$).

The single absorption band is the $t_{2g}\to e_{g}$ transition of this electron, so its energy equals the splitting: $\Delta _{o}=20300\text{cm}^{-1}$.

$\text{CFSE}=-0.4\Delta _{o}=-0.4\times 20300=-8120\text{cm}^{-1}$

With $1\text{kJ mol}^{-1}=83.7\text{cm}^{-1}$:

$\text{CFSE}=-\dfrac{8120}{83.7}\text{kJ mol}^{-1}=-97\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

The stabilization energy is thus $97\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ in magnitude.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
The total number of monohalogenated organic
products in the following (including
stereoisomers) reaction is $______$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The simplest optically active alkene is 3-methylpent-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, whose C-3 carries H, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$ and the vinyl group.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}/\mathrm{Ni}$ gives 3-methylpentane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, which is achiral and has four kinds of hydrogen.

Halogen on a terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ of an ethyl group: $\mathrm{XCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (1-halo-3-methylpentane), one stereocentre, 2 stereoisomers.

Halogen on a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$: $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CHXCH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (2-halo-3-methylpentane), two different stereocentres, 4 stereoisomers.

Halogen on the $\mathrm{CH}$: $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CX}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (3-halo-3-methylpentane), achiral, 1 product.

Halogen on the branch $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: $\mathrm{XCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ (1-halo-2-ethylbutane), achiral, 1 product.

Total number of monohalogenated products $=2+4+1+1=8$.

Hence, the answer is 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
The photoelectric current from Na (Work function, $w_{0}$
 = 2.3 eV) is stopped by the output voltage of
the cell
 $Pt(s) | H_{2}$
(g, 1 Bar) | HCl (aq., pH =1) | AgCl(s) | Ag(s).

The pH of aq. HCl required to stop the photoelectric current from $K(w_{0}$
 = 2.25 eV), all other
conditions remaining the same, is $_______$ $\times$ $10^{-2} ($to the nearest integer).

Given, 2.303$\frac{RT}{F}$ = 0.06 V;

$E_{AgCl|Ag|Cl^{-}}^{0}$ = 0.22 V
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{1}{2}H_{2} +$ AgCl $\to$ $H^{+} + Ag + Cl^{-}$

From Nernst Equation,

$E_{$cell} = $E_{cell}^{0}$ - $\frac{0.06}{1}\log [H^{+}][Cl^{-}]$

$= 0.22 – 0.06 \log  10^{–2} = 0.34 V$

Work function of Na metal = 2.3 eV

KE of photoelectron = 0.34 eV

Energy of incident radiation = 2.3 + 0.34 = 2.64 eV

For K atom,

Energy of incident radiation for K metal
= 2.64 eV

Work function of K metal = 2.25 eV

KE of photoelectrons = 2.64 – 2.25 = 0.39 eV

$\therefore$ $E_{$cell} = 0.39 V

Using Nernst Equation,

0.39 = 0.22 - $\frac{0.06}{1}\log [H^{+}][Cl^{-}]$

As $[H^{+}]=[Cl^{-}]$

0.39 = 0.22 - $\frac{0.06}{1}\log [H^{+}]^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 0.39 = 0.22 - $0.12\times \log [H^{+}]$

$\Rightarrow$ 0.39 = 0.22 + 0.12 $\times$ pH

$\Rightarrow$ pH = 1.42 = 142 $\times$ $10^{-2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot
